title: A Protein That Clamps Itself Off

scenes.tts: Can a protein read its own tail? Sark does. A fatty acid, myristate, anchors Sark to the inner face of the plasma membrane. Then come an S H 3 domain, an S H 2 domain, a linker, the kinase domain, and a short tail. The tail holds tyrosine five twenty-seven, six residues from its end.
scenes.caption: Can a protein read its own tail? Src does. A fatty acid, myristate, anchors Src to the inner face of the plasma membrane. Then come an SH3 domain, an SH2 domain, a linker, the kinase domain, and a short tail. The tail holds tyrosine 527, six residues from its end.
scenes.visual: A bare bar with a dashed question arrow from its tail end back toward its start. The bar fills in as named: myristate anchor to the membrane, SH3, SH2, linker, kinase, tail, tyrosine 527.
scenes.narration: Can a protein read its own tail? Src does. A fatty acid, myristate, anchors Src to the inner face of the plasma membrane. Then come an SH3 domain, an SH2 domain, a linker, the kinase domain, and a short tail. The tail holds tyrosine 527, six residues from its end.

scenes.tts: The enzyme C S K puts a phosphate on that tyrosine. The tail folds back. The protein's own S H 2 domain grips the phosphotyrosine. Its own S H 3 domain grips the linker. Both settle on the back of the kinase and hold it inactive.
scenes.caption: The enzyme Csk puts a phosphate on that tyrosine. The tail folds back. The protein's own SH2 domain grips the phosphotyrosine. Its own SH3 domain grips the linker. Both settle on the back of the kinase and hold it inactive.
scenes.visual: Csk adds a phosphate badge to the tail end. The row folds into a compact shape; the SH2 cup closes on the badge, the SH3 cup closes on the linker; an inactive label appears.
scenes.narration: The enzyme Csk puts a phosphate on that tyrosine. The tail folds back. The protein's own SH2 domain grips the phosphotyrosine. Its own SH3 domain grips the linker. Both settle on the back of the kinase and hold it inactive.

scenes.tts: The clamp is deliberately loose. The tail fits the S H 2 pocket poorly, so a better ligand can pull it away. A phosphorylated P D G F receptor does this. So does the kinase F A K, once integrins have switched it on. A proline-rich partner such as beta-arrestin can take the S H 3 domain. Once open, the kinase phosphorylates tyrosine four sixteen in its own activation loop, and stays active.
scenes.caption: The clamp is deliberately loose. The tail fits the SH2 pocket poorly, so a better ligand can pull it away. A phosphorylated PDGF receptor does this. So does the kinase FAK, once integrins have switched it on. A proline-rich partner such as beta-arrestin can take the SH3 domain. Once open, the kinase phosphorylates tyrosine 416 in its own activation loop, and stays active.
scenes.visual: The closed clamp is marked loose. A better ligand (PDGF receptor, then FAK) takes the SH2 cup and the tail swings free; beta-arrestin takes the SH3 cup and the linker is pushed out. Tyrosine 416 on the activation loop gets a phosphate and the kinase turns active.
scenes.narration: The clamp is deliberately loose. The tail fits the SH2 pocket poorly, so a better ligand can pull it away. A phosphorylated PDGF receptor does this. So does the kinase FAK, once integrins have switched it on. A proline-rich partner such as beta-arrestin can take the SH3 domain. Once open, the kinase phosphorylates tyrosine 416 in its own activation loop, and stays active.

scenes.tts: The viral protein, v Sark, has lost the tail, and tyrosine five twenty-seven with it. The S H 2 domain has nothing to grip, so the clamp never forms. Changing tyrosine five twenty-seven to phenylalanine in c Sark does the same, and makes it transform cells. The viral form is always on because it has lost its off-switch.
scenes.caption: The viral protein, v-Src, has lost the tail, and tyrosine 527 with it. The SH2 domain has nothing to grip, so the clamp never forms. Changing tyrosine 527 to phenylalanine in c-Src does the same, and makes it transform cells. The viral form is always on because it has lost its off-switch.
scenes.visual: c-Src closed and off. The tail and its tyrosine vanish (v-Src): empty cup, clamp open, active. Then c-Src with tyrosine 527 changed to F: same result. Finally the off-switch is crossed out.
scenes.narration: The viral protein, v-Src, has lost the tail, and tyrosine 527 with it. The SH2 domain has nothing to grip, so the clamp never forms. Changing tyrosine 527 to phenylalanine in c-Src does the same, and makes it transform cells. The viral form is always on because it has lost its off-switch.
